concepts.why: The presence of thin-walled, irregularly branched blood vessels and positive immunohistochemistry results for CD31 and CD34 support the diagnosis of Kaposi's sarcoma.

The clinical presentation of multiple, firm, nonscaly, purple erythematous patches and plaques with irregular borders, along with the histopathological findings of thin-walled, irregularly branched blood vessels, supports the diagnosis of hemangioma.
The patient's history of intracranial hemorrhage, family history of similar conditions, and detection of a heterozygous pathogenic KRIT1 variant support this diagnosis.

The presence of multiple bluish, partially keratotic papules and nodules on the lower legs, sonography demonstrating intradermal slow-flow vascular malformations, and biopsy revealing dilated venous-like malformations support this diagnosis.
The patient's history of lipolymphedema of the lower legs attributed to functional venous insufficiency supports this diagnosis.

concepts.why: The presence of a heterogeneous mass with solid and cystic components in the left maxillary sinus, along with the displacement of the inferior rectus muscle and the absence of cytologic atypia, suggests a diagnosis of Juvenile Nasopharyngeal Angiofibroma.

The presence of mild left-sided proptosis and the displacement of the inferior rectus muscle suggests a diagnosis of Orbital Tumor.

concepts.why: The patient's progressive unilateral skin hardening, ill-defined plaque, and loss of skin elasticity, along with the histopathological findings of increased density of fibroblasts and dense reticular dermis, are consistent with scleroderma.
The patient's unilateral skin hardening, ill-defined plaque, and hypertrichosis are consistent with morphea, a form of localized scleroderma.
The patient has a left-sided lacrimal sac abscess with postseptal fat stranding and increased abscess size with globe compression.
The patient has edematous, hyperemic left eyelids, diffuse limitation in extraocular movements, and a left-sided lacrimal sac abscess.
The patient has acute injury to the entire orbital segment of the left optic nerve as shown by diffusion-weighted imaging.
The patient has several months of epiphora without prior dacryocystitis.
The patient has initial cultures isolated gram-positive cocci in chains, later identified as pan-susceptible Streptococcus pyogenes.

facts.raw_span: 2-year history of multiple, slowly growing, infiltrated erythematous-violaceous patches and plaques
occasional slight pain extending from her left upper arm to the left side of her chest
No triggers such as local infection, insect bite, or trauma occurred before lesion appearance

Multiple firm, nonscaly, purple erythematous patches and plaques with irregular borders on her left axilla, medial upper arm, and lateral thoracic region

Thin-walled, irregularly branched blood vessels dispersed between thickened collagen bundles
Endothelial cells were plump but displayed no significant cytologic atypia
Positive for: CD31, CD34, Ki-67 (<1%)
Negative for: podoplanin (D2-40), human herpesvirus 8 (HHV-8)

Image D Description: Endothelial cells positive for cluster of differentiation (CD) 31
multiple (approximately 10) bluish, partially keratotic papules and nodules on the lower legs
The lesions had been growing very slowly in number and size since age 24
had been bleeding occasionally after trauma
right-sided hemiparesis and hemianopsia caused by an intracranial hemorrhage
recurrent seizures at age 4
